authoredNote: Source written first from the #868 pre-declared contract (decorator metadata for javascript: attached, referenced at the decorator's own line, never a call/read of the enclosing scope, and kept on an EXPORTED class whose decorator the grammar puts on the wrapping export_statement). The numbers below were then read off the post-fix run and agree with the fixture's own text (`@sealed` 46 / `export class Service` 47, `@inject(DB)` 48 / `pool = make()` 49, `@sealed` 51 / `method() {}` 52, `@inject("getter")` 54 / `get value()` 55).
rationale: M49 (#868), javascript half of the web family's decorator contract, on one shape. FOUR things are pinned. (1) A FIELD's decorator is attached — the class and method paths called the own-child collector and the field path never did, so `pool` carried no decorator while the identical typescript shape yielded decorators=["inject"]. (2) Every decorator's name is a `references` edge FROM the decorated symbol at the DECORATOR's own line (46/48/51/54), never the declaration's (47/49/52/55) — each decorator is on a different line from the name it decorates, so the near-miss answer is a different number, and the name list is `metadata.decoratorLines`, parallel to `decorators` (the M59 #860 lockstep the typescript twin already has). (3) A decorator is METADATA, not a call or a read by whoever encloses it: `@inject(DB)` used to emit `calls Service -> inject` from the class that carries it, and the bare-read pass emitted `uses Service -> sealed` / `uses method -> sealed`, i.e. a class appearing to call and read a decorator it never mentions in its body; the family rule (typescript's `inDecoratorPosition`, JVM annotations as metadata, the python oracle's PYD1) leaves only the reference edges. (4) An EXPORTED class keeps its decorator: this grammar puts the class decorator on the wrapping export_statement when the class is exported (`export_statement [decorator@46, export@47, class_declaration@47]`), where the own-child reader never looked, so `@sealed export class Service` used to produce NO decorator entry and NO reference edge at all. DISCRIMINATION built into the text so a too-broad rule fails instead of passing: `make()` in the field INITIALIZER is a genuine call and must survive, and the getter's body must still emit its own read — decorator position is positional, not 'anything near a decorator'. 2026-10-18 CANONICAL VOCABULARY: the decorator rows are `decorates` now (RelationshipType.Decorates, landed in src/ast/types.ts df5a03eb2), not `references`: source = the decorated declaration, target = the decorator name leaf, line = the decorator's own line, one row per decorator and none for a decorator's arguments. The four near-miss forbids moved with the label so borrowing the declaration's line still fails.
